hypotheses_queue.observation: Word and character TF-IDF are high-performing (19.2% and 15.1%), but real multi-lingual cross-lingual semantic equivalence (e.g. Hindi/French business descriptors) can benefit from a lightweight dense offline embedding.
hypotheses_queue.hypothesis: Adding cosine similarity from an offline, lightweight sentence-transformer (all-MiniLM-L6-v2) as a 17th feature will provide semantic representation without compromising 100% local execution.
hypotheses_queue.falsification_test: Verify that feature importance incorporates semantic similarity without slowing feature extraction by more than 3x.

history.finding: F0.5 jump from 0.84 to 0.91 was caused by silent .replace() bug leaking identical addresses, not parser.
Auditing all generator .replace() calls established genuine adversarial baseline at 0.8644.
Generalized trailing number regex recovered 18 abbreviated French street numbers, lifting F0.5 to 0.9167.
Unicode NFKD accent stripping + dotted initial collapse + international legal forms boosted F0.5 to 0.9233.
Evaluated on independent 10,000-record public FEBRL4 benchmark without cheat IDs: achieved 0.9507 Macro F0.5, 95.07% Precision, 95.07% Recall, and 0 False Merges.

Evaluated on real-world Fodors-Zagat corporate restaurant/chain benchmark (533 businesses, 423 singletons): achieved 100.00% blocking recall, 100.00% test recall, 99.54% precision, and 0.9959 Macro F0.5.

Added sublinear character 3-5 gram TF-IDF cosine within word boundaries (tfidf_char_cosine). Successfully decentralized feature reliance: word TF-IDF dropped from 25.0% to 19.2%, while char TF-IDF captured 15.1% of splits. No single feature now exceeds 19.2%.
